1.2 Install and build

The Python comparison needs Python 3.12 or newer, ExifTool, NumPy, tifffile and imagecodecs. The project pins its dependency set through uv. Native Rust targets Unix and is pinned to Rust 1.99.0, edition 2024. The metadata pool is written in ordinary OCaml. Its historical executable name ends in -oxcaml so existing archives and backend selection remain compatible; that name does not require an OxCaml compiler. The OCaml byte worker’s C SHA binding uses macOS CommonCrypto.

On macOS, install uv and rustup using their official installation instructions, then install the remaining tools and build:

brew install exiftool xdelta ocaml
git clone https://github.com/firstpair/dng-compare.git
cd dng-compare
make setup
rustup toolchain install 1.99.0
make build
make test

Run these from the real repository root. make setup uses uv sync; ordinary Python commands use uv run python. Do not substitute a different Rust release without recording and testing that change. Confirm the compilers you actually use:

uv run python --version
rustc --version
ocamlopt -version
exiftool -ver
xdelta3 -V

make build-rust builds the ordinary Rust binaries. make build-oxcaml builds metadata-extract-oxcaml and byte-verify-oxcaml. The Makefile defaults to OCAMLOPT=ocamlopt and accepts an explicit compiler or flags override:

make build-oxcaml OCAMLOPT=/path/to/ocamlopt OCAMLFLAGS=-O3

The older OXCAMLOPT override remains available for an existing switch. Linux can use the Python comparator and Unix Rust tools when their dependencies are available; the macOS CommonCrypto OCaml byte binding needs a platform-specific replacement there. Native Windows support is not supplied by these Unix file, process and lock APIs.

The tests create temporary synthetic files. They check comparison, cache invalidation, preservation, bounded parallel work and checkpoint behavior. A passing fixture suite is evidence for those cases, not validation of every camera, codec or DNG layout. Optional Turso probes are separate from the normal build and are discussed below. The publication validation record names the observed compilers, fixture results and remaining untested scopes.
